transcript: First off, the job of the Planning Commission is to make recommendations based on the comprehensive plan to draw out things, for example, like the light tonight, which we brought up with the roads, so that the Board of Supervisors can make, because they make the final decisions. We make recommendations. It goes forward. We've had recommendations go forward where it's 13-0 our way, and it's going 7-0 the other way. It's our job to draw out and gain this information. We spent a year on this, working on the NEIL. The staff's done a wonderful job. There's been a lot of people putting in time. Rather than taking it back to CPPC, what if we send to the Board what the working group recommended, what the CPPC recommended, and what the staff recommended, and let the Board take a look at it and see what they're going to come back, because they're eventually going to kick it back to us anyway. It would be nice if everybody had... Correct information, because that's not been evident here. I was going to say that, John. I was going to say, if we do that, if we send all three things, they're going to kick it right back. They're going to kick it back no matter what. They're going to kick it back no matter what, but at least the staff has a chance to present what a year's worth of work has gone into here at the different levels of what's been recommended. Then we could probably go to CPPC. But then we... We get feedback from the Board. I understand what you're saying, and that probably is a good option. But then are we doing our job if we do that? We're kind of throwing our hands up, and maybe that's where we are. We're throwing our hands up saying, we don't know what to do. You guys decide. Now, they have to make the final decision anyhow. Ultimately, they get paid the big bucks for that. They're elected. But if we took another... And I don't know. Could the CPPC and staff come up with a consolidated plan in another one or two meetings? I mean, what are we talking about? We're talking a month or two? I wouldn't want it to drag out six months because, just like you said, things get stale. If we draw it out six months, we might as well trash it and start over. So if one or two meetings would make a difference, I'm glad to give it a shot. But again, that's up to you guys. I'm just one person up here. Yeah. What I would just add again is your all's opinions are extremely important to how this progresses from our perspective. So if it is the will of the commission to bring it back to CPPC, there's no hard and fast rules that I have to continue this on its course to the board. If that's the way this body feels, I'll gladly redirect and bring it back to the CPPC for further consideration. Well, let's go right down the line here then. I would suggest that it go back to the CPCC, whatever all those letters are. It should really only be three. Oh, is it? But it is CPPC. All right. Well, let's start. Ms. Brimbach? I would agree. Mr. Barker, you agree? I agree. I agree. Ms. Dawson? I agree. I agree. I agree. I agree. I agree. I agree as well. I agree. I agree. You all agree. Looks like we'll be sitting in the CPPC evenings. Absolutely. Thank you all for your thoughtful comments and reading the plan. As always, I very much respect your opinions and appreciate the feedback on it. Mr. Pearson, the staff's done a wonderful job. We appreciate the work that's gone into this. This is not something that's easy. It's a life balance here because, like Mr. Thomas said, we're talking about some people's livelihood. Folks own property, and we need to be able to take care of doing the right thing there. So everything that's gone into it, just how much it's appreciated. Thank you. Thank you very much. Mr. Shaw, are you happy to answer any current plans? I'm happy to answer any applications, questions that you all may have. I don't have any worthy applications to name for the commission, but I know that's next on your agenda. So I'm happy to answer any. So I'm looking for a motion to adjourn. So moved. Look at that. That was a good one. We're adjourned. That was a good discussion. Thank you.
